rubrics.justification: Describes an expanded Day 5 blastocyst with thinned zona, compact ICM, and cohesive TE consistent with the reported 3AA grade; appropriately notes limits of a single static image. Slightly inferential beyond what can be confirmed from one image, so not perfect.
Thoroughly integrates age, BMI, ovarian reserve markers, oocyte yield, unexplained diagnosis, prior failed cycle, semen parameters, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: strong embryo morphology and very young age improve prognosis, while obesity and prior failed cycle modestly temper expectations. Probability estimates are clearly tied to these factors.

Recommendations are well aligned with IVF practice standards: elective single embryo transfer in a very young patient with a good-quality blastocyst, caution against routine PGT-A/ERA/immune testing after limited failures, and appropriate attention to transfer technique and luteal support.

Provides practical next steps for transfer, monitoring, and future evaluation if failure recurs, including cavity review and metabolic optimization. Useful and specific, though some recommendations remain general rather than protocol-level.
